neighbours.label: the word just before an expected 'the air' (love is in | the air, fired into | the air, moisture from | the air): anticipates 'air'
fire: Spring has arrived and there is a feeling of love in the air.
The soldier raised his rifle and fired three shots into the air.
Clouds form when water vapour condenses from the air above us.
The scent of fresh bread drifted through the air of the market.
After the goal, the fans threw their scarves into the air.
With the holidays near, excitement was in the air all week.
The kite rose high up into the air on the windy hill.
The smell of smoke hung in the air long after the fire.
quiet: Spring has arrived and there is a box of flowers in the hallway.
The soldier raised his rifle and fired three shots at the target.
Clouds of dust rose when the truck drove onto the gravel road.
The scent of fresh bread came from the bakery near the market.
After the goal, the fans threw their scarves onto the pitch.
With the holidays near, the shops were busy all week.
The kite got stuck in the branches of a tall tree.
The smell of smoke stayed in our clothes long after the fire.

notes: Top examples peak on in/into/from/fill before 'the air'; output promotes air, atmosphere, sky. The - pole fires on 'air' itself / 'the air we breathe'.
